findings.reason: apply.js:85 computes toPos = oldStart + offset + diffOffset - 1, which is -1 when oldStart is 0. The fit loop at :61-66 accepts that position because hunkFits has no context lines to check for a pure-add hunk. With the clamp gone, splice(-1, 0, ...) at :101 inserts before the last element: 'line2\nline3\n' becomes line2,line3,line1 and '' gives reversed lines. That breaks the locked tests at test/patch/apply.js:396, :411, :635 and :709. acceptance.md has no numbered AC, so breaks is set to story; the locked-tests bar is the one missed.
findings.claim: Removing the toPos < 0 clamp makes hunks with oldStart 0 (new-file creation, insertion at start of file) apply at index -1. The output gets corrupted and the locked baseline tests for these cases fail.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (toPos < 0) { // Creating a new file\n toPos = 0; }`. For `@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@`, `toPos = hunk.oldStart + hunk.offset + diffOffset - 1` = -1. On source '' (`lines` = ['']), the first '+' runs `lines.splice(-1, 0, 'line1')`, which inserts before the last element and gives ['line1',''], then `toPos++` makes it 0. Each later '+' then splices at index 0 ahead of the earlier lines, so the result is line4,line3,line2,line1. `delimiters.splice(-1, …)` is misaligned in the same way. hunkFits never rejects this position because a pure-add hunk has no context lines to compare.
